causal_claim.content: Restoring inversion symmetry in the bilayer produces a hidden Rashba effect with local RSOC canceling globally.
causal_claim.evidence_span: In this bilayer, inversion symmetry is restored, giving rise to a hidden Rashba effect [29, 30], where RSOC exists locally within each layer but cancels out globally due to inversion symmetry.

causal_claim.content: Structural relaxation causes significant lattice reconstruction and spatially modulated registries.
causal_claim.evidence_span: During structural relaxation, the twisted bi- layers undergo significant lattice reconstruction, resulting in spatially modulated atomic registries across the moir´e supercell.

causal_claim.content: Continuous modulation of interlayer separation directly determines local topological character.
causal_claim.evidence_span: As shown in Figures. 2(b) and 2(e), the optimized structures exhibit a continuous modulation of the interlayer separation d, which directly determines the local topological character, as reflected in the Z2 phase diagrams [Figs. 2(c) and 2(f)].

causal_claim.content: Twisting alone drives a topological phase transition.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This is a concrete example of a topological phase transition that is purely driven by twisting.

causal_claim.content: Vertical alignment of Sb atoms in AA increases pz overlap, causing strong repulsion and larger interlayer separation.
causal_claim.evidence_span: In the AA stacking, the vertical alignment of Sb atoms leads to significant overlap of the out-of-plane Sb–pz orbitals [as shown in Figure 1(d)], resulting in strong interlayer re- pulsion and, consequently, a large interlayer separation of approximately 3.7 ˚A.

causal_claim.content: Lateral displacement of Sb atoms in AB reduces overlap and repulsion, yielding smaller interlayer separation.
causal_claim.evidence_span: In contrast, the AB stacking, where Sb atoms are laterally displaced, minimizes orbital over- lap, reducing interlayer repulsion and yielding a smaller separation of about 2.1 ˚A ; see Supplementary Fig. 1(b) for details.

causal_claim.content: Small interlayer spacing in AB strengthens tunneling and yields a nontrivial topological phase; large spacing in AA reduces tunneling and leaves it trivial.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Consequently, the AB stacking, which exhibits the smallest interlayer spac- ing, shows the strongest electron tunneling and exhibits a topologically nontrivial phase (Z2 = 1). In contrast, AA stacking, characterized by the largest interlayer separa- tion, exhibits reduced tunneling and remains topologically trivial (Z2 = 0) in their optimized configuration.

causal_claim.content: Structural relaxation creates spatial variation in interlayer distance through lattice reconstruction and local stackings.
causal_claim.evidence_span: However, struc- tural relaxation induces spatial variations in the interlayer distance due to lattice reconstruction, resulting in locally distinct stacking configurations.

causal_claim.content: Lower twist angle increases nontrivial-domain fraction because relaxation maximizes low-energy AB domains.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This arises because, during structural relaxation, the 9.43◦twisted bilayer significantly maximizes the AB domains in the optimized structure, owing to the lower energy of the AB stacking configuration.

causal_claim.content: Probing below the Fermi level excludes edge states so boundary high-LDOS features disappear.
causal_claim.evidence_span: In contrast, probing further below EF excludes these edge states, leaving only bulk trivial states, so no high-LDOS features appear along the boundaries of the nontrivial regions.

causal_claim.content: Increasing field to about 0.10–0.15 eV/Å makes all stackings trivial, switching edge channels OFF.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Increas- ing the field strength to approximately 0.10–0.15 eV/˚A renders all stacking configurations trivial, corresponding to a complete OFF state of the conducting edge channels in the moir´e supercell.

causal_claim.content: Further increasing the field restores nontrivial domains, switching edge channels back ON.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Upon further increasing the field, nontrivial domains reemerge, effectively turning the edge channels back to the ON state.

causal_claim.content: Across an isolated M=0 contour, a helical Kramers pair localized at the domain wall appears.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Across an isolated M = 0 contour, a single chiral Dirac mode appears in a single time-reversal fixed sector, while its partner adds the counter-propagating mode in the second sector. Together, they form a helical Kramers pair localized within a characteristic length scale ξ(r) ≃ ℏv / |M(r)| at the domain wall [35].

causal_claim.content: Structural relaxation strongly renormalizes Vc and Vs and makes AB and BA inequivalent with distinct local Z2 character.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Structural relaxation, captured by our first-principles calculations, strongly renormalizes the values of Vc and Vs, and naturally incorporates the mirror-symmetry breaking between different stacking regions. As a result, the AB and BA domains become inequivalent and acquire dis- tinct local Z2 character.

causal_claim.content: Smooth spatial variation of M(r) allows multiple helical edge channels to merge at boundaries between trivial and nontrivial domains.
causal_claim.evidence_span: At the same time, the smooth spatial variation of M(r) enables multiple helical edge channels to merge at the boundaries of topologically triv- ial and nontrivial domains.

causal_claim.content: The mass distribution includes a component that flips sign when twist direction is reversed, revealing chiral origin.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This mass distribution, contains a component which flips sign with reversing the twist direction, directly revealing its chiral origin [Figs. 5(a)-(b)].

causal_claim.content: Interplay of moiré reconstruction, interlayer hybridization, and SOC generates a spatially textured topological landscape instead of a uniform phase.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Rather than producing a uniform topological phase, the interplay of moir´e recon- struction, interlayer hybridization, and spin-orbit coupling generates a spatially textured topological landscape in which topologically nontrivial and trivial regions coexist within a single moir´e unit cell.

causal_claim.content: Local stacking environment controls the sign and magnitude of effective mass M(r), making topology real-space dependent.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This establishes a “topo- logical mosaic” in which the local stacking environment directly controls the sign and magnitude of an effective mass term M(r), making topology intrinsically real-space dependent.

causal_claim.content: Chemical substitution with more electronegative elements reduces semimetallicity, opens a gap, and drives the system toward a semiconducting regime.
causal_claim.evidence_span: However, as we demonstrate in the Supplementary Figure S5, this semimetallicity can be systematically reduced through chemical substitution with more electronegative elements such as iodine or fluorine, which open a band gap and drive the system toward a semiconducting regime.

causal_claim.content: Relaxation-driven modulation of interlayer separation stabilizes topological phase separation in moiré matter.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Relaxation-driven modulation of in- terlayer separation plays a central role in stabilizing this phase separation in moir´e matter.

mechanism_principle.content: AA has strong Sb-pz overlap, which causes interlayer repulsion and larger spacing.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: In the AA stacking, the vertical alignment of Sb atoms leads to significant overlap of the out-of-plane Sb–pz orbitals [as shown in Figure 1(d)], resulting in strong interlayer re- pulsion and, consequently, a large interlayer separation of approximately 3.7 ˚A.

mechanism_principle.content: AB minimizes orbital overlap, lowering interlayer repulsion and spacing.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: In contrast, the AB stacking, where Sb atoms are laterally displaced, minimizes orbital over- lap, reducing interlayer repulsion and yielding a smaller separation of about 2.1 ˚A ; see Supplementary Fig. 1(b) for details.

mechanism_principle.content: Strong Sb-pz repulsion leaves Bi-pz orbitals dominant near the Fermi level, and stacking controls Bi-pz hybridization and tunneling via spacing.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Owing to the strong Sb–pz orbital repulsion, the elec- tronic states near the Fermi level are primarily contributed by the Bi–pz orbitals. Since the stacking configuration strongly influences the interlayer separation, it directly governs the degree of hybridization and interlayer electron tunneling between the Bi–pz orbitals.

mechanism_principle.content: At lower energies, bulk states dominate, which removes the edge-state STM signature.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: the edge-state signature vanishes due to the dominance of bulk states.

mechanism_principle.content: The electric field both enhances interlayer tunneling and shifts bands near the Fermi level, suppressing band inversion and driving triviality.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: It is worth noting that the electric field plays a dual role here: (i) it enhances the out-of-plane interlayer tunneling, driving the topological phase transition [28], and (ii) it shifts the bands near the Fermi level that are responsible for topological band inversion. As these bands are pushed away from the Fermi level, the band inversion vanishes and the system transitions into a topologically trivial phase.

mechanism_principle.content: Asymmetry between inequivalent sites comes from the relative magnitudes of Vs and Vc producing slightly larger positive mass where edge states percolate.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The observed asymmetry between inequivalent sites originates from the relative magnitude of Vs and Vc, which produces a slightly larger positive (trivial) mass in regions where the edge states percolate.

hypothesis_statement.content: Topological domain size can be controlled by adjusting twist angle.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: This suggests that the size of the topological domains in BiSb-SbBi bilayers can be effectively controlled by adjusting the twist angle.

hypothesis_statement.content: STM is proposed as an experimentally feasible method to probe spatially distributed topological domains.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: To explore an experimentally feasible method for probing the spatially distributed topological domains in the moir´e supercell, we simulated STM images for all three twist angles.

hypothesis_statement.content: STM can directly probe emergent edge states in moiré-induced topological domains.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: This establishes STM as a direct probe of emergent edge states in moir´e-induced topological domains.

hypothesis_statement.content: An external electric field can be used as a tunable control knob for the moiré topological character.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: An external electric field can serve as a tunable knob to control the topological character of the moir´e supercell.

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors propose a minimal continuum model capturing the essential physics seen in DFT.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: here we provide a conceptual model that captures all the essential physics emerging from full DFT calculations. We propose a minimal continuum model reflecting the strong SOC and the natural composition of Bi-pz orbitals in the low energy sector of the (untwisted) system [28].

hypothesis_statement.content: Scanning probe measurements can reconstruct the spatial mass profile from LDOS data.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Taken together, these results demonstrate that scanning probe measurements can be used to reconstruct the spatial mass profile M(r) from LDOS data

hypothesis_statement.content: The framework offers a route to reconstruct moiré topological landscapes and extract mass-texture parameters using gate-tunable STM.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Combined with gate-tunable STM measurements, our framework provides an innovative route to reconstructing the topological landscape of moir´e bands and extracting the under- lying parameters governing the spatial mass texture M(r).

hypothesis_statement.content: Structural relaxation is proposed as a fundamental mechanism reshaping topology in twisted vdW heterostructures.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Our results establish structural relaxation as a fundamental mechanism that reshapes topology in twisted vdW heterostructures.

hypothesis_statement.content: Real-space approaches are necessary for characterizing topology in moiré systems because local stacking switches topological regimes.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: In particular, the spatial modulation of M(r) demonstrates how local stacking environments can act as nanoscale switches between distinct topological regimes, emphasizing the need for real-space approaches when characterizing topology in moir´e systems.

hypothesis_statement.content: Relaxation is identified as a design principle for reconfigurable topological networks and devices in vdW materials.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: More broadly, our results identify relaxation as a powerful design principle for engineering reconfigurable topological networks in vdW materials, opening pathways toward intrinsically patterned topolog- ical circuits and planar device architectures.

evidence_result.content: The untwisted bilayer is topologically nontrivial while the monolayer is trivial.
evidence_result.evidence_span: While the mono- layer is topologically trivial (Z2 = 0), the untwisted bilayer is topologically nontrivial (Z2 = 1) [28].

evidence_result.content: Relaxed moiré supercells preserve threefold rotational symmetry but break inversion symmetry.
evidence_result.evidence_span: For all three twist angles, the relaxed moir´e supercells crystallize in the p312 symmetry (layer group no. 67), containing 28, 76, and 128 atoms for the 21.78◦, 13.17◦, and 9.43◦twist angles, respectively. While inversion symmetry is broken in the moir´e supercell, the threefold rotational symmetry is preserved.

evidence_result.content: A 60° Bernal-stacked bilayer remains topologically trivial without spatially varying topology.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Notably, at larger twist angles such as 60◦, which correspond to Bernal stacking, the optimized bilayer remains topolog- ically trivial and does not exhibit any spatially varying topological character (see Supplementary Fig. S2).

evidence_result.content: AB stacking is energetically most favorable and AA is least favorable by about 0.5 eV.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Among all configurations, AB stacking is the most energetically favorable, whereas AA stacking is the least favorable, lying approximately 0.5 eV higher in energy.

evidence_result.content: AB regions have the smallest interlayer separation, AA the largest, with distances spanning about 2.1 to 3.2 Å.
evidence_result.evidence_span: AB-stacked regions exhibit the smallest interlayer separation, whereas AA-stacked regions have the largest. Overall, the interlayer distance across the supercell ranges approximately from 2.1 ˚A to 3.2 ˚A.

evidence_result.content: Spatial Z2 maps show AA regions are trivial and AB regions nontrivial.
evidence_result.evidence_span: As expected, AA stacking regions with the largest interlayer separation are topologically trivial (Z2 = 0, shown in gray), whereas AB domains with the smallest interlayer separation exhibit a nontrivial phase (Z2 = 1, blue regions).

evidence_result.content: Reducing twist angle from 13.17° to 9.43° raises the nontrivial-domain fraction from about 49% to about 70%.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Notably, reducing the twist angle from 13.17◦to 9.43◦increases the Z2 = 1 domain fraction from ∼49% to approximately 70% of the total area.

evidence_result.content: Near the Fermi level, STM shows high LDOS along boundaries of Z2=1 domains, matching localized edge states.
evidence_result.evidence_span: For the 13.17◦twist angle, probing near the Fermi level reveals highly local density of states (bright yellow) along the boundaries of the Z2 = 1 domains at their interfaces with Z2 = 0 regions, corresponding to edge states localized at the boundaries of topologically nontrivial domains.

evidence_result.content: For 9.43°, enhanced LDOS near EF traces domain-wall edge states, but at lower energies the signature vanishes.
evidence_result.evidence_span: A similar behavior is observed for the 9.43◦ twist angle. Enhanced LDOS near EF (EF ± 0.15 eV) traces the domain-wall edge states, while at lower energies (EF - 0.8 eV to EF - 1.0 eV) the edge-state signature vanishes due to the dominance of bulk states.

evidence_result.content: At 60° Bernal stacking, no edge-state-induced LDOS enhancement is seen, consistent with trivial topology.
evidence_result.evidence_span: However, at the larger twist angle of 60◦corresponding to Bernal stacking, no such edge-state-induced LDOS enhancement is observed, consistent with its topologically trivial character (see Fig. S2 in the Supplementary Information).

evidence_result.content: At zero field the moiré supercell contains both trivial and nontrivial domains.
evidence_result.evidence_span: As shown in Fig. 4(a), at zero field, the AB domain is topologically nontrivial, while the remaining stacking pat- terns exhibit a mixture of trivial and nontrivial domains. Consequently, the moir´e supercell hosts both Z2 = 1 and Z2 = 0 domains in the absence of an applied field.

evidence_result.content: Estimated parameters give ξ ~ 0.1 nm, placing the system in the sharp edge-state-network regime.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Using ℏv = 120 meV·nm along with a typical mass scale |M| ∼1 eV, which is consistent with the strength of interorbital repulsion in this system [28], we obtain ξ ∼ 0.1 nm, placing the system well within the sharp edge- state network regime.

evidence_result.content: The model reproduces an inverted mass distribution and honeycomb-like pattern consistent with moiré C3v symmetry.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We find an expected inverted mass distribution and a honeycomb-like pattern reflect- ing the underlying C3v symmetry of the moir´e lattice.

evidence_result.content: LDOS near zero energy shows pronounced 1D edge states along boundaries between trivial and nontrivial domains, while domains remain gapped.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We then compute the LDOS, near E ≈0, and plot it in Figs. 5(c)-(d). We observe pronounced one-dimensional edge states which emerge precisely along the boundaries separating topolog- ically nontrivial and trivial domains, whereas the domains themselves remain gapped and exhibit zero DOS (pur- ple hue).

evidence_result.content: LDOS maps change clearly when twist chirality is reversed, enabling real-space probing of local moiré chirality.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Importantly, the LDOS maps display a clear contrast under reversal of the twist chiral- ity, providing a direct real-space probe of the local moir´e chirality.

evidence_result.content: Continuum calculations identify an extended window of topological bands below charge neutrality and a broad trivial occupied sector.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We identify an extended energy window with topological bands below the charge neutrality point, spanning an energy range of approximately Vc below EF . We then show the existence of a broad trivial sector of occupied bands.

evidence_result.content: These continuum results match the coexistence of topological and trivial regions seen in DFT.
evidence_result.evidence_span: These results match the observed coexistence of topological and trivial regions identified in DFT calculations shown in Fig. 3(b).

evidence_result.content: Twisting and structural relaxation create a spatially varying topological phase landscape from two trivial monolayers.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We have demonstrated that twisting and structural relaxation in BiSb bilayers provide a route to programmable topological matter in moir´e systems. Start- ing from two individually trivial monolayers (Z2 = 0), inversion-stacked and twisted bilayers develop a spatially varying topological phase landscape characterized by co- existing topologically nontrivial (Z2 = 1) and trivial (Z2 = 0) domains.

evidence_result.content: The continuum BHZ-type model reproduces real-space topology and links STM observables to the spatial mass term.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Our continuum BHZ-type description, informed by first- principles calculations, reproduces the real-space topology and establishes a direct connection between STM observ- ables and the underlying spatially varying mass term M(r).

evidence_result.content: Twist angle tunes domain size and electric field reversibly controls edge-state connectivity.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The ability to tune domain size via twist angle and reversibly control edge-state connectivity using an electric field demonstrates a high degree of exter- nal programmability.

constraint.content: A sharp edge-state network requires localization length much smaller than moiré periodicity.
constraint.evidence_span: The observation of a sharp edge-state network implies ξ ≪aM, where aM is the moir´e periodicity.

constraint.content: A caveat is that pristine BiSb bilayers are semimetallic with trivial electron/hole pockets near the Fermi level.
constraint.evidence_span: A caveat that is worth noting in pristine BiSb bilayers is that these are semimetallic in nature, with some topologically trivial electron/hole pockets lying near the Fermi level.

hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: This suggests that the size of the topological domains in BiSb-SbBi bilayers can be effectively controlled by adjusting the twist angle.

hypothesis_statement.content: STM is proposed as an experimentally feasible method to probe spatially distributed topological domains.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: To explore an experimentally feasible method for probing the spatially distributed topological domains in the moir´e supercell, we simulated STM images for all three twist angles.

hypothesis_statement.content: STM can directly probe emergent edge states in moiré-induced topological domains.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: This establishes STM as a direct probe of emergent edge states in moir´e-induced topological domains.

hypothesis_statement.content: An external electric field can be used as a tunable control knob for the moiré topological character.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: An external electric field can serve as a tunable knob to control the topological character of the moir´e supercell.

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors propose a minimal continuum model capturing the essential physics seen in DFT.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: here we provide a conceptual model that captures all the essential physics emerging from full DFT calculations. We propose a minimal continuum model reflecting the strong SOC and the natural composition of Bi-pz orbitals in the low energy sector of the (untwisted) system [28].

hypothesis_statement.content: Scanning probe measurements can reconstruct the spatial mass profile from LDOS data.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Taken together, these results demonstrate that scanning probe measurements can be used to reconstruct the spatial mass profile M(r) from LDOS data

hypothesis_statement.content: The framework offers a route to reconstruct moiré topological landscapes and extract mass-texture parameters using gate-tunable STM.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Combined with gate-tunable STM measurements, our framework provides an innovative route to reconstructing the topological landscape of moir´e bands and extracting the under- lying parameters governing the spatial mass texture M(r).

hypothesis_statement.content: Structural relaxation is proposed as a fundamental mechanism reshaping topology in twisted vdW heterostructures.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Our results establish structural relaxation as a fundamental mechanism that reshapes topology in twisted vdW heterostructures.

hypothesis_statement.content: Real-space approaches are necessary for characterizing topology in moiré systems because local stacking switches topological regimes.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: In particular, the spatial modulation of M(r) demonstrates how local stacking environments can act as nanoscale switches between distinct topological regimes, emphasizing the need for real-space approaches when characterizing topology in moir´e systems.

hypothesis_statement.content: Relaxation is identified as a design principle for reconfigurable topological networks and devices in vdW materials.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: More broadly, our results identify relaxation as a powerful design principle for engineering reconfigurable topological networks in vdW materials, opening pathways toward intrinsically patterned topolog- ical circuits and planar device architectures.

evidence_result.content: The untwisted bilayer is topologically nontrivial while the monolayer is trivial.
evidence_result.evidence_span: While the mono- layer is topologically trivial (Z2 = 0), the untwisted bilayer is topologically nontrivial (Z2 = 1) [28].

evidence_result.content: Relaxed moiré supercells preserve threefold rotational symmetry but break inversion symmetry.
evidence_result.evidence_span: For all three twist angles, the relaxed moir´e supercells crystallize in the p312 symmetry (layer group no. 67), containing 28, 76, and 128 atoms for the 21.78◦, 13.17◦, and 9.43◦twist angles, respectively. While inversion symmetry is broken in the moir´e supercell, the threefold rotational symmetry is preserved.

evidence_result.content: A 60° Bernal-stacked bilayer remains topologically trivial without spatially varying topology.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Notably, at larger twist angles such as 60◦, which correspond to Bernal stacking, the optimized bilayer remains topolog- ically trivial and does not exhibit any spatially varying topological character (see Supplementary Fig. S2).

evidence_result.content: AB stacking is energetically most favorable and AA is least favorable by about 0.5 eV.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Among all configurations, AB stacking is the most energetically favorable, whereas AA stacking is the least favorable, lying approximately 0.5 eV higher in energy.

evidence_result.content: AB regions have the smallest interlayer separation, AA the largest, with distances spanning about 2.1 to 3.2 Å.
evidence_result.evidence_span: AB-stacked regions exhibit the smallest interlayer separation, whereas AA-stacked regions have the largest. Overall, the interlayer distance across the supercell ranges approximately from 2.1 ˚A to 3.2 ˚A.

evidence_result.content: Spatial Z2 maps show AA regions are trivial and AB regions nontrivial.
evidence_result.evidence_span: As expected, AA stacking regions with the largest interlayer separation are topologically trivial (Z2 = 0, shown in gray), whereas AB domains with the smallest interlayer separation exhibit a nontrivial phase (Z2 = 1, blue regions).

evidence_result.content: Reducing twist angle from 13.17° to 9.43° raises the nontrivial-domain fraction from about 49% to about 70%.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Notably, reducing the twist angle from 13.17◦to 9.43◦increases the Z2 = 1 domain fraction from ∼49% to approximately 70% of the total area.

evidence_result.content: Near the Fermi level, STM shows high LDOS along boundaries of Z2=1 domains, matching localized edge states.
evidence_result.evidence_span: For the 13.17◦twist angle, probing near the Fermi level reveals highly local density of states (bright yellow) along the boundaries of the Z2 = 1 domains at their interfaces with Z2 = 0 regions, corresponding to edge states localized at the boundaries of topologically nontrivial domains.

evidence_result.content: For 9.43°, enhanced LDOS near EF traces domain-wall edge states, but at lower energies the signature vanishes.
evidence_result.evidence_span: A similar behavior is observed for the 9.43◦ twist angle. Enhanced LDOS near EF (EF ± 0.15 eV) traces the domain-wall edge states, while at lower energies (EF - 0.8 eV to EF - 1.0 eV) the edge-state signature vanishes due to the dominance of bulk states.

evidence_result.content: At 60° Bernal stacking, no edge-state-induced LDOS enhancement is seen, consistent with trivial topology.
evidence_result.evidence_span: However, at the larger twist angle of 60◦corresponding to Bernal stacking, no such edge-state-induced LDOS enhancement is observed, consistent with its topologically trivial character (see Fig. S2 in the Supplementary Information).

evidence_result.content: At zero field the moiré supercell contains both trivial and nontrivial domains.
evidence_result.evidence_span: As shown in Fig. 4(a), at zero field, the AB domain is topologically nontrivial, while the remaining stacking pat- terns exhibit a mixture of trivial and nontrivial domains. Consequently, the moir´e supercell hosts both Z2 = 1 and Z2 = 0 domains in the absence of an applied field.

evidence_result.content: Estimated parameters give ξ ~ 0.1 nm, placing the system in the sharp edge-state-network regime.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Using ℏv = 120 meV·nm along with a typical mass scale |M| ∼1 eV, which is consistent with the strength of interorbital repulsion in this system [28], we obtain ξ ∼ 0.1 nm, placing the system well within the sharp edge- state network regime.

evidence_result.content: The model reproduces an inverted mass distribution and honeycomb-like pattern consistent with moiré C3v symmetry.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We find an expected inverted mass distribution and a honeycomb-like pattern reflect- ing the underlying C3v symmetry of the moir´e lattice.

evidence_result.content: LDOS near zero energy shows pronounced 1D edge states along boundaries between trivial and nontrivial domains, while domains remain gapped.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We then compute the LDOS, near E ≈0, and plot it in Figs. 5(c)-(d). We observe pronounced one-dimensional edge states which emerge precisely along the boundaries separating topolog- ically nontrivial and trivial domains, whereas the domains themselves remain gapped and exhibit zero DOS (pur- ple hue).

evidence_result.content: LDOS maps change clearly when twist chirality is reversed, enabling real-space probing of local moiré chirality.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Importantly, the LDOS maps display a clear contrast under reversal of the twist chiral- ity, providing a direct real-space probe of the local moir´e chirality.

evidence_result.content: Continuum calculations identify an extended window of topological bands below charge neutrality and a broad trivial occupied sector.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We identify an extended energy window with topological bands below the charge neutrality point, spanning an energy range of approximately Vc below EF . We then show the existence of a broad trivial sector of occupied bands.

evidence_result.content: These continuum results match the coexistence of topological and trivial regions seen in DFT.
evidence_result.evidence_span: These results match the observed coexistence of topological and trivial regions identified in DFT calculations shown in Fig. 3(b).

evidence_result.content: Twisting and structural relaxation create a spatially varying topological phase landscape from two trivial monolayers.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We have demonstrated that twisting and structural relaxation in BiSb bilayers provide a route to programmable topological matter in moir´e systems. Start- ing from two individually trivial monolayers (Z2 = 0), inversion-stacked and twisted bilayers develop a spatially varying topological phase landscape characterized by co- existing topologically nontrivial (Z2 = 1) and trivial (Z2 = 0) domains.

evidence_result.content: The continuum BHZ-type model reproduces real-space topology and links STM observables to the spatial mass term.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Our continuum BHZ-type description, informed by first- principles calculations, reproduces the real-space topology and establishes a direct connection between STM observ- ables and the underlying spatially varying mass term M(r).

evidence_result.content: Twist angle tunes domain size and electric field reversibly controls edge-state connectivity.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The ability to tune domain size via twist angle and reversibly control edge-state connectivity using an electric field demonstrates a high degree of exter- nal programmability.

constraint.content: A sharp edge-state network requires the localization length to be much smaller than the moiré periodicity (ξ ≪ aM).
evidence_spans: The observation of a sharp edge-state network implies ξ ≪aM, where aM is the moir´e periodicity.

constraint.content: A caveat/constraint is that pristine BiSb bilayers are semimetallic, with topologically trivial electron and hole pockets near the Fermi level.
evidence_spans: A caveat that is worth noting in pristine BiSb bilayers is that these are semimetallic in nature, with some topologically trivial electron/hole pockets lying near the Fermi level.
